cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), and he just told them they're not under law but under grace (Romans 6:14). Now he turns to his brothers who know the law, which is basically Paul saying, "Okay, rule people, this one's for YOU." Then he asks how long the law gets a say over a person.

cards.question: How long does Paul say the law has authority over a man?

answers.text: Only as long as he lives
Only as long as he lives in Israel

cards.text: Then Paul gives a picture every grown-up can follow: marriage. A married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives.

cards.question: In Paul's marriage picture, if the husband dies, the woman is still bound by the law of marriage.

cards.text: Paul spells it out like he's reading the fine print nobody ever reads. If she's joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she's called an adulteress.

cards.question: But if her husband dies and she marries another man, Paul says she is not an ___.

cards.text: Now Paul brings the picture home, and whoa, I did NOT see who was dying in this one. You also died to the law, he tells his brothers, through the body of Christ.

cards.question: Paul says the believers died to the law so they could belong to someone new. Who?

answers.text: Him who was raised from the dead
Moses who gave them the law
Abraham the father of us all

cards.question: Paul says belonging to the risen Christ means we might bear fruit to ___.

cards.text: Then Paul looks back at when we lived according to the flesh, and sinful passions were at work in our bodies. AT WORK, friend: clocked in early, stayed late, never once called in sick.

cards.question: Paul says those sinful passions at work in our bodies were aroused by the ___.
Paul says those sinful passions were bearing fruit for death.

cards.text: But now, Paul says, we've died to what bound us and been released from the law. RELEASED, friend, and I say that as a guy who sat in a junk drawer so long the dust had a seating chart.

cards.question: Now that they're released from the law, how does Paul say believers serve?

answers.text: In the new way of the Spirit
In the old way of the written code
In the strict way of the elders

cards.text: Then Paul throws a question at his own letter: "What then shall we say? Is the law sin?" Friend, I respect a man who heckles HIMSELF.

cards.question: Paul says the law is sin.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law." The law's like the friend who points at your shirt and says, "Uh, you got something there," and NOW you can't stop seeing it.

cards.question: Paul gives one example of a sin he wouldn't have been aware of if the law hadn't named it. Which one?

cards.text: Then Paul says sin seized its opportunity through the commandment. It's like a sign that says DO NOT TOUCH, and suddenly your hand is hovering there like it's got a mind of its own.

cards.question: Paul says sin, through the commandment, produced in him every kind of ___ desire.
Paul says that apart from the law, sin is dead.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died." Sin SPRANG to life, like the worst surprise party ever, jumping out the second the commandment walked in.

cards.question: What does Paul discover about the commandment that was meant to bring life?

cards.text: Paul explains how, and there's that line again: sin seized its opportunity through the commandment. Leave sin one little gap and it's IN, like the car that merges the second you let a foot open up in traffic.

cards.question: What does Paul say sin did to him through the commandment before it put him to death?

cards.text: So is the commandment the bad guy here, or is sin the one using it? You don't blame the stamper when somebody else presses crooked, and I say that AS a stamper.

cards.question: So then, Paul says the law is ___.

cards.text: Then Paul asks one more: did that which is good become death to him? "Certainly not!" he says, for the second time, and friend, this man is NOT letting the good guy take the fall.

cards.question: So why does Paul say sin produced death in him through something good?

answers.text: So sin would be exposed as sin
So the law would look stronger
So Paul would learn to obey

cards.question: Paul says that through the commandment, sin might become utterly sinful.

findings.problem: The joke puts a made-up line in Paul's mouth ('Okay, rule people, this one's for YOU'). It makes fun of the people he is writing to, the 'brothers who know the law,' by calling them 'rule people.' The humor laughs at a group in the passage, not with their human situation.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Only until he turns forty' is silly next to the others, so it's easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke compares Paul's words to 'the fine print nobody ever reads.' That makes Scripture the target of the joke and suggests the passage is something people skip.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: Story card 5 says 'she's called an adulteress' right before this card. Card 6 then asks the baker to fill in 'not an ___.' The setup gives away the answer word, and 'outsider' and 'servant' plainly don't fit the marriage setup.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'holy' and 'gentle' aren't believable as a desire that sin produces. Card 4 has already set up coveting, so the right answer is the only one that makes sense.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: Story card 8 has just quoted 'sin sprang to life and I died' about the commandment coming. That rules out the wrong answers 'It actually brought peace' and 'It actually brought joy' before the baker reasons at all.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card tells no part of the passage. It is only a setup question and a joke about the stamper, so the passage doesn't move forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites Romans 7:11, but it tells nothing from that verse. What it hints at, that the commandment isn't to blame, comes from Romans 7:12-13.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Romans 7:12 says the commandment is 'holy, righteous, and good.' No card tells that the commandment is righteous and good. Card 14 says 'that which is good' without linking it to the commandment, so the baker misses a key detail of Paul's conclusion.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
